A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RRM research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved from v1's appendix into v2's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model and policy evaluations, a Neutrals ablation, response-length analyses and an injected-artifact experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Gemma-2-2b-it evaluations and a mixed-artifact robustness experiment in Appendices A.5–A.6.

M1.justification: The pairwise reward model, Non-contextuals and Neutrals augmentation in Equation 5, augmentation filtering rule, and policy procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 proposes safety filtering for future work; it does not implement a new method component.

E1.justification: The eight-source training mixture and Reward-Bench, MT-Bench and AlpacaEval-2 coverage remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 adds a distinct contamination scenario involving boldface and emoji during training and emoji during evaluation, alongside the retained prefix-artifact scenario.

E2.justification: RM, ODIN and the -Neutrals variant retain their participation in the corresponding original comparisons. The added smaller-model and mixed-artifact experiments compare RM with RRM without introducing another comparison method; newly discussed ensembles are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the reported reward-model training duration from 'until convergence' to one epoch, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. Appendix A.5 adds 2B reward models ranking 9B-generated responses, while A.6 specifies a new contamination protocol with 10% boldface and 10% emoji injection during training.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 and Figure 7 add a robustness test asking whether RRM resists emoji selection after training with mixed boldface/emoji artifacts. The original Neutrals ablation, length analyses and single-prefix artifact experiment remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for its experiments. The added tables and figure continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original results in v1 Tables 1–2 remain unchanged in v2 Tables 2–3. New Tables 4–5 report 2B RM/RRM Reward-Bench averages of 71.01/72.25 and AlpacaEval-2 length-controlled win rates of 44.21/54.37 for BoN-8 and 47.32/60.42 for BoN-64. Figure 7 adds mixed-artifact findings; these are additional settings, not revisions to the original scores.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly states the sufficiency assumption P(C|X,Y1,Y2)=P(C|S,A), variable domains and the assumption that rejected contextual responses remain acceptable. Proposition 3.1's example now writes conditional preference probabilities. Both propositions and their proof arguments already appeared in v1; moving the proofs into Section 3 does not constitute new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual preference disentanglement, causal augmentation and improved induced policies. Their headline numerical comparisons are unchanged; the new appendix experiments provide additional support.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 substantially qualifies the central premise: prompt-independent safety preferences can be legitimate, and augmentation can promote unsafe rejected responses or label safe/unsafe pairs as ties. It identifies concrete failure conditions and proposes future safety-model or AI-feedback filtering. Section 4.2 also narrows the asserted MT-Bench advantage to the first turn.

D1.justification: v2 specifies one epoch as the selected reward-model training duration and adds a reproducibility statement promising training and experiment code upon publication, without supplying a release link. The augmentation code example, ODIN implementation details and dataset access links were already present in v1 and are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Coste et al. on reward-model ensembles and Stiennon et al. on learning from human feedback, with a short expansion of related-work discussion. The new Bai et al. 2022c entry duplicates the Constitutional AI work already cited as 2022b; the central positioning against existing approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Section 3.2 under explanatory subheadings, moves the proofs and dataset composition into the main text, and expands the appendices with analyses, discussion and statements. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact, with localized clarification and language corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5 and the two-panel Figure 7, and relocates v1's dataset-composition Table 3 as main-text Table 1. Existing plots and table structures are retained, alongside modest figure resizing, page reflow and conference headers.

improvement.justification: The smaller-model and mixed-artifact experiments modestly broaden support, while Appendix A.7 makes an important safety limitation explicit and Section 4.2 corrects the overly broad MT-Bench comparison. These gains outweigh a local inconsistency: A.5 claims Safety regresses although Table 4 reports 72.70 to 72.71. The method and original results remain unchanged, and the proposed safety remedies are not tested.
